chapter_title: Chương 81: Bắt Đầu Kỳ Thi Đại Học

segments.title: Chương 81: Bắt Đầu Kỳ Thi Đại Học
segments.content:
There was a rain shower yesterday, and the summer heat temporarily retreated.

But after a night, I woke up to a big, bright sun again. Thankfully, it wasn't as muggy as the past few days.

Rows of brand-new buses were parked on the open ground outside the school gate.

A few teachers who weren't assigned to invigilate stood in front of the buses, shouting repeatedly: "Check your things. Have you brought your ID and admission ticket? Have you brought your 2B pencils..."

Occasionally, a forgetful student or two, upon hearing the teachers' repeated reminders, would cry out "Damn!" and turn around to run back.

The group from dorm room 302 moved together, filing onto the bus.

Some people on the bus were joking around thoughtlessly, but most of the students were solemn and silent. A few who had suffered from insomnia last night closed their eyes for a nap as soon as they got on.

Once a bus was full, it would depart immediately, without waiting for the others.

The bus started moving slowly; the driver drove very steadily.

Xie Yang said in a low voice: "I only started studying seriously this past month. Damn, don't tell me I can't even get into a tier-two university?"

"Stay calm, don't be nervous," Chen Guiliang said.

Xie Yang clenched his fists: "I always thought I wouldn't get nervous. But I almost had insomnia last night and didn't fall asleep until after one in the morning."

Chen Guiliang pointed to the side and front, lowering his voice to a whisper: "Don't say things like that, you'll make Yang Hao even more nervous. That kid probably really did have insomnia, he even had dark circles under his eyes this morning."

"Hah!"

Xie Yang let out a breath and leaned back in his seat, closing his eyes to rest.

The examination center they were heading to was at the new campus of the County No. 1 High School. The bus ride was only about ten minutes.

The area outside the exam center was filled with students and parents, some of whom had arrived as early as two hours beforehand.

Chen Guiliang got off the bus with the crowd, only to hear Xie Yang joking around with Li Yulin and Wang Yu.

"You're not nervous anymore?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Xie Yang smiled: "I'm okay. It's the same blade whether you stick your neck out or pull it in."

Chen Guiliang turned his head to look at Yang Hao and saw him trembling slightly. He thought to himself: This kid is done for. Just like in my last life, he'll underperform and only get into a tier-three university.

His mental fortitude is too poor!

Xu Haibo, on the other hand, was relatively calm. He had exceeded the tier-one university cutoff score by more than 30 points in three consecutive mock exams.

His phone's text message alert chimed.

It was from Bian Guanyue: "Good luck!"

"Good luck!" Chen Guiliang replied.

Two days before the Gaokao, Bian Guanyue had returned to Rongcheng. Her school registration was there.

Just after sending the text to Bian Guanyue, Chen Guiliang received another one from Tao Xue.

"Big Nephew, good luck!"

"Thanks, Auntie Xue."

Rongcheng.

A Mercedes-Benz drove through the old city district.

Bian Guanyue looked at the text message and smiled faintly. She quickly regained her composure, leaning back in her seat to rest and conserve her energy.

Bian Jinsong glanced at his daughter's fleeting smile in the rearview mirror and guessed she was probably texting Chen Guiliang.

As a father, how could he possibly throw his daughter into a small county town and not care?

He even knew about his daughter's close relationship with Chen Guiliang.

Bian Jinsong had also secretly donated 500,000 yuan to the school, part of which was to subsidize students from poor families, and part to reward top students. If Chen Guiliang could get into Peking University, a portion of the prize money from the school would come from Bian Jinsong's donation.

"Don't be nervous, stay calm," Bian Jinsong said.

Bian Guanyue said: "I know, don't disturb my rest."

Bian Jinsong wanted to say more but held his tongue, obediently shutting his mouth.

If he hadn't helped her pick up her admission ticket, his daughter probably wouldn't have been very willing to see him on this trip back to Rongcheng.

Bian Jinsong was a Rongcheng native, born and raised. He graduated from a teachers' college and was a teacher for two years.

At that time, Bian Guanyue's mother, Guan Xiaolin, had joined the Rongcheng Sichuan Opera Troupe as an actress. With Bian's parents playing matchmaker, Bian Jinsong and Guan Xiaolin fell in love and got married.

Amidst the great wave of reform, Bian Jinsong resigned to go into business, but his development wasn't very smooth.

While doing business, he met a widow.

Not only was she as beautiful as a flower, but both of her parents were also officials.

The widow pursued him, and Bian Jinsong simply couldn't resist. This widow was too understanding, whereas his wife at home was unreasonable.

Gradually, he spent less and less time at home and more and more time with the widow.

The affair was exposed, the couple had huge fights, and finally reached the point of divorce.

Only later did he find out that the widow... that is, his second wife, had secretly used some tricks to frequently provoke his ex-wife into a rage.

His second wife was no simple character!

Bian Jinsong's business grew bigger and bigger, but he was suppressed more and more by his wife, who also had the majority share in the company. It wasn't until his official father-in-law passed away from illness that he could finally breathe a little, but by then, his and his wife's careers were already bound together.

He didn't even dare to hire a beautiful female secretary, fearing his wife would cause a scene at the company again. In the end, he simply switched to a male secretary.

Sometimes, Bian Jinsong also regretted his choice back then.

But he only regretted marrying that widow, not divorcing his ex-wife. Given his ex-wife's strange temper, he figured they would have divorced sooner or later, with or without a third party.

His two marriages were just a matter of jumping from one pit into another.

"Mr. Bian, there's a traffic control ahead, we'll need to get out and walk a bit," the driver reminded, then suddenly added, "It seems you can pass if you show an admission ticket."

Bian Jinsong said: "Find a place to pull over and park."

The father and daughter walked towards the examination center. There were still more than 40 minutes before the exam began.

They weren't allowed into the exam center yet, so the two stood outside in silence.

"I'll leave so I don't annoy you." Bian Jinsong planned to leave first.

Bian Guanyue thought for a moment: "It's fine."

A flicker of joy lit up Bian Jinsong's heart, and he quickly returned to stand by his daughter's side. He didn't say anything more, just stood there until he watched his daughter walk into the examination center.

He was extremely worried.

People always talked about how competitive Henan and Shandong provinces were, but the college admission rates of these two provinces were always ahead of Sichuan's.

Sichuan ranked near the bottom!

Firstly, there were too many exam takers, and secondly, the rate of students repeating the year was particularly high.

Take the County No. 2 High School for example. There were fewer than 1,000 graduating third-year students, but there were also about 160 students repeating the year.

It was very difficult for Bian Guanyue to give up the art school exam path in her third year.

Chen Guiliang found his exam room and seat, handed his phone to the invigilator, returned to his seat to arrange his exam materials, and then rested his head on the desk for a nap.

Before long, the exam papers were distributed.

The invigilator said: "Don't start writing yet. First, fill in your candidate information. In previous years, there were some candidates who did very well on the exam but forgot to write their names!"

Two or three minutes later, the exam officially began.

Question 1: Choose the correct Pinyin pronunciation for the following words: 执著, 结束, 妊娠, 言简意赅.

Very easy.

Question 2: Select the group of words with no typos.

Relatively easy, but easy to make a mistake.

Question 3: Also relatively easy, but also easy to make a mistake.

Chen Guiliang had long forgotten the Gaokao questions from that year. His feeling now doing the Chinese language paper was that it was relatively easy but full of potential traps.

For the average student, as long as they were careful, there wouldn't be any major problems. Only the last few written questions were slightly difficult—

Translate the classical Chinese text into modern Chinese. 8 points. Relatively difficult.

Analyze and understand a ci poem by Yan Jidao. 6 points. Extremely difficult.

Write a transitional script for a radio station's tourism weather forecast. 6 points. Relatively difficult.

Complete a couplet. 4 points. Relatively difficult.

These 24 points worth of questions allowed for a high degree of freedom. As long as the answers weren't too far off the mark, it was easy to get the basic points, but getting a high score required an exceptional performance.

Essay prompt: Happiness and Our Way of Thinking.

What essay did I write in my last life?

Chen Guiliang couldn't remember for the life of him.

He didn't rush to start writing the essay. Instead, he went back and carefully checked all the previous questions and his answers, taking the opportunity to adjust his mood and train of thought.

After checking, he corrected one multiple-choice question.

Then he laid out his draft paper and began to brainstorm for the essay.

After thinking for five or six minutes, Chen Guiliang wrote down the essay title: Where Thoughts Turn, Flowers Bloom.

The main idea of the essay was: Happiness is a subjective feeling, which one may not possess even in favorable circumstances. Especially in adversity, people often become pained and negative. At this time, one must break through mental barriers and face the world with a different mindset. Even in adversity, one can discover happiness.

For a Gaokao essay, you have to show off your learning, packing it with famous quotes and anecdotes about remarkable people and events.

The introduction and conclusion had to be concise and brilliant, because the grading teacher would look at your beginning and end first. Only if they found it impressive would they read the middle content carefully.

People like Tao Yuanming and Su Dongpo, just throw them all in, along with their poems about discovering happiness in ordinary life or adversity.

Finally, he would add a chicken soup-style conclusion: "Life is unpredictable, and little is certain. By embracing life with a grateful heart and facing difficulties with a calm mind, happiness will emerge in every little moment. As long as one breaks through the barriers of thought, in the turn of a mind, wastelands can bloom, and cages can transform into the open sky."

It was greasy and schmaltzy, but Gaokao essays had to be like that.

After copying the essay from the draft paper, there was still half an hour left until the end of the exam.

Chen Guiliang checked his answers one more time and felt he could probably score over 140 on the Chinese exam this time.

Handing in his paper 15 minutes early, Chen Guiliang strolled out of the examination center.

On his way, he met two staff members helping a female student towards the school gate, heading straight for the ambulance parked outside.

After the girl got into the ambulance, Chen Guiliang asked: "What happened to her?"

A staff member answered: "She got menstrual cramps from nervousness right when the exam started. She held on until she finished her essay, but then the pain was so bad she fell to the floor and couldn't get up."

Chen Guiliang scratched his head.

From time to time, familiar classmates left the exam hall. Some of them forgot the teachers' instructions and started comparing answers right after coming out. Looking for trouble.

Two minutes later, Xie Yang walked out of the exam center with a relaxed look on his face, seeming to have done quite well.

Xie Yang said with a smile: "The Chinese exam was so easy. I worried for nothing."

"What did you choose for the second question?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"A," Xie Yang said.

Chen Guiliang nodded: "A is the right choice, you got it."

Right, my ass. Xie Saobang fell right into the trap!

But this was not the time to dampen his spirits.

The questions for each subject this year were probably similar: most were simple but easy to fall for traps, with a few more difficult ones specifically designed to separate the scores.
